pr.title: Fix login timeout on slow networks
pr.author: demo-contributor

evidence.text: The issue stack points to validate in src/auth/authService.js and reports an expired session.
The PR changes dispatch and adds retryDispatch.
The issue anchors createSession, isExpired, and validate are not touched by this PR.
dispatch is a high-degree hub on the login, profile, and health request paths and may affect seven dependent nodes.
Issue-area hit is false and graph relevance is 0 for non-test touched nodes.
retryDispatch is a new definition and is not present in the base-commit graph.

assessment.claim_summary: The PR claims the five-second request timeout causes the session-expiry report and raises it to 30 seconds with retry-safe dispatch.
assessment.reality_summary: The change affects timeout and routing code, while the issue points to session expiry code that this PR does not touch.

findings.text: None of the issue-anchored session functions are changed.
The PR changes dispatch, a high-degree request hub that may affect unrelated routes.
The new retryDispatch helper is not mapped in the base graph.

tests.name: session remains valid after five seconds
tests.reason: Directly checks the issue symptom against the session-expiry path.

questions_for_contributor: What evidence connects the request timeout to the session expiration reported in validate?
Can you add a regression test that waits past five seconds and verifies the session remains valid?

priorityReason: The mapped changes miss the issue area and have zero graph relevance; ask for evidence connecting timeout handling to session expiry.
